intro: Hi! Today you learn to describe people: what they look like (tall, long black hair, glasses) and what they are like (friendly, patient, funny). Then you compare them: My brother is taller than me. Warm-up: think of your best friend. Is he or she tall or short?
teachingNotes: Appearance uses two verbs. be + adjective for height and body (She's tall, He's slim); have/has (got) + adjective + noun for hair, eyes, a beard or a moustache (She has long hair, He has a beard). Common errors: *'She is long hair', *'She has hair long' (Indonesian 'rambut panjang' puts the adjective after the noun), *'He is beard'. For people 'tinggi' is tall, never high. Glasses, a hijab, a watch: wear = pakai (He wears glasses, not *'uses glasses'); glasses always has -s.

Hair on the head is uncountable: *'long black hairs' is wrong ('a hair' is one single strand, e.g. in your food; only mention it if asked). eyes has -s because eyes are counted. Order: length first, colour last (long black hair, short grey hair); straight/curly goes in the middle (long straight black hair). Only build exercises on length + colour, because the order of curly/straight and colour is sometimes heard both ways. grey/moustache are British, gray/mustache American.

Personality words: friendly (ramah), kind (baik hati), funny (lucu, makes you laugh), shy (pemalu), lazy (malas), hard-working (rajin), honest (jujur), patient (sabar). With a noun you need a: *'He is very friendly person' → He is a very friendly person (or He is very friendly). a/an looks at the next word: an honest man (silent h) but a very honest man. Traps: 'lucu' for a baby or a kitten is cute, not funny; 'baik hati' is kind or nice ('She's good' usually means good at something). Soften negative words: a bit lazy, not very patient.

What does she look like? = appearance (answer with is/has: She's tall and she has curly hair). What is she like? / What's she like? = personality, what kind of person (She's friendly and very funny). What does she like? = what she likes (She likes music). In the first two 'like' means 'seperti', not 'suka'. Don't let learners answer *'She looks like tall'. look like + a person = mirip (Rina looks like her mother).

Be respectful. 'fat' is rude in English even though 'gemuk' is said casually in Indonesia: teach a bit heavy or big, and slim (a compliment) vs thin (can sound 'too thin'). Never joke about bodies, never describe skin colour, don't use 'ugly'. Keep examples kind and about real Indonesian people (family, colleagues, neighbours).

Comparing people reuses a2-comparatives; don't re-teach the -er/more rules from scratch, just apply them: taller/younger/older/kinder/shorter than, funnier/lazier, more patient/more honest, the tallest in my family, as tall as, not as patient as. After than, 'me' is normal (accept 'than I am'). kakak/adik = older/younger sister/brother. Avoid friendly, shy and hard-working in comparative exercises (friendlier/more friendly, shyer/shier: two forms). Limits: present only: no past simple, no will, no present perfect.

keyPoints.title: Appearance: be or have
keyPoints.explanation: Use be + adjective for height and body: She's tall. He's slim. Use have/has + adjective + noun for hair, eyes and a beard: She has long hair (not 'hair long'). Two describing words: length first, colour last: long black hair. hair has no -s. For glasses use wear: He wears glasses. Be polite: say a bit heavy, not fat.

examples.en: My father has short grey hair.

id.title: Penampilan: be atau have
id.explanation: Pakai be + kata sifat untuk tinggi badan dan bentuk tubuh: She's tall. He's slim. Pakai have/has + kata sifat + kata benda untuk rambut, mata, dan jenggot: She has long hair (bukan 'hair long'). Dua kata sifat: panjang dulu, warna terakhir: long black hair. hair tidak diberi -s. Untuk kacamata pakai wear: He wears glasses. Sopanlah: bilang a bit heavy, bukan fat.

keyPoints.title: Personality: What is she like?
keyPoints.explanation: Personality words: friendly, kind, funny, shy, lazy, hard-working, honest, patient. Use them after be (She's patient) or before a noun with a: She's a very friendly person (not 'very friendly person'). What is she like? asks about personality. What does she look like? asks about appearance. Here like means 'seperti', not 'suka'.

examples.en: What's your teacher like? — She's kind and very patient.
examples.id: Gurumu orangnya seperti apa? — Dia baik hati dan sangat sabar.

examples.en: What does your new colleague look like? — He's short and he wears glasses.
examples.id: Rekan kerja barumu penampilannya seperti apa? — Dia pendek dan pakai kacamata.

examples.en: Pak Hasan is a very honest man.
examples.id: Pak Hasan orang yang sangat jujur.

id.title: Sifat: What is she like?
id.explanation: Kata-kata untuk sifat: friendly, kind, funny, shy, lazy, hard-working, honest, patient. Pakai setelah be (She's patient) atau sebelum kata benda dengan a: She's a very friendly person (bukan 'very friendly person'). What is she like? menanyakan sifat. What does she look like? menanyakan penampilan. Di sini like artinya 'seperti', bukan 'suka'.

keyPoints.title: Compare people
keyPoints.explanation: Use the comparative rules you know. Short words: -er + than (taller than, younger than, kinder than). Words with 2 beats ending in -y: funnier, lazier. Longer words: more patient, more honest. After than, say me: My brother is taller than me. The same: as tall as. Not the same: not as patient as.

examples.en: My brother is two years older than me.
examples.id: Kakakku dua tahun lebih tua daripada aku.

examples.en: My mother is more patient than my father.
I'm not as tall as my sister.

id.title: Membandingkan orang
id.explanation: Pakai aturan perbandingan yang sudah kamu tahu. Kata pendek: -er + than (taller than, younger than, kinder than). Kata 2 ketukan berakhiran -y: funnier, lazier. Kata yang lebih panjang: more patient, more honest. Setelah than, pakai me: My brother is taller than me. Sama: as tall as. Tidak sama: not as patient as.

material.title: Tall, slim, a beard: is or has?

blocks.text:
To describe how someone looks (their **appearance**, *penampilan*), English uses two verbs:
- **be + adjective** for height and body: *Rina **is** tall. Budi **is** slim.* (An **adjective** is a describing word, *kata sifat*.)
- **have/has + adjective + noun** for hair, eyes, a beard or a moustache: *Rina **has** long hair. Budi **has** a beard.* (A **noun** is the name of a thing, *kata benda*.)

Indonesian *Rina tinggi* has no verb, but English needs **is**: **Rina is tall**. And for people, *tinggi* is **tall**, not *high*.

For glasses (and a hijab, a watch, clothes) use **wear** = *pakai*: **He wears glasses.** Not 'uses glasses': *use* is for tools, like a phone or a computer. **glasses** always has -s (two lenses).

id.text:
Untuk menjelaskan penampilan seseorang (**appearance**, *penampilan*), bahasa Inggris memakai dua kata kerja:
- **be + kata sifat** untuk tinggi badan dan bentuk tubuh: *Rina **is** tall. Budi **is** slim.* (**Adjective** = kata sifat, kata yang menggambarkan.)
- **have/has + kata sifat + kata benda** untuk rambut, mata, jenggot atau kumis: *Rina **has** long hair. Budi **has** a beard.* (**Noun** = kata benda, nama sesuatu.)

Kalimat *Rina tinggi* tidak punya kata kerja, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh **is**: **Rina is tall**. Dan untuk orang, *tinggi* adalah **tall**, bukan *high*.

Untuk kacamata (juga hijab, jam tangan, pakaian) pakai **wear** = *pakai*: **He wears glasses.** Bukan 'uses glasses': *use* untuk alat, seperti HP atau komputer. **glasses** selalu pakai -s (dua lensa).

id.note: short = pendek (untuk badan dan juga rambut)

blocks.text: **Be polite about bodies.** In Indonesia people often say *gemuk* or *kurus* quite openly. In English **fat** sounds rude, so say **a bit heavy** or **big**, or don't mention it. **slim** (*langsing*) is a compliment; **thin** (*kurus*) can sound like 'too thin'. And don't describe someone's skin colour or make jokes about their body.

id.text: **Sopan saat membicarakan tubuh.** Di Indonesia orang sering bilang *gemuk* atau *kurus* dengan terang-terangan. Dalam bahasa Inggris **fat** terdengar kasar, jadi bilang **a bit heavy** (*agak gemuk*) atau **big**, atau tidak usah disebut. **slim** (*langsing*) adalah pujian; **thin** (*kurus*) bisa terdengar seperti 'terlalu kurus'. Dan jangan mendeskripsikan warna kulit seseorang atau bercanda tentang tubuhnya.

blocks.explain: Height is a describing word on its own, so use **be**: Dimas **is** tall. Use **has** only with a noun (has a beard, has long hair). And no **a** before an adjective on its own.

id.explain: Tinggi badan adalah kata sifat yang berdiri sendiri, jadi pakai **be**: Dimas **is** tall. Pakai **has** hanya dengan kata benda (has a beard, has long hair). Dan tidak ada **a** sebelum kata sifat yang berdiri sendiri.

id.title: Tinggi, langsing, berjenggot: is atau has?

blocks.text:
Indonesian puts the describing word **after** the noun: *rambut panjang*. English puts it **before**: **She has long hair** (or **Her hair is long**). Never 'She has hair long' or 'She is long hair'.

With two describing words, use a fixed order: **length first, colour last**: **long black hair**, **short grey hair**. If you add **straight** (*lurus*) or **curly** (*keriting*), it goes in the middle: **long straight black hair**.

The **hair** on your head has **no -s**: *long black hair*, not 'long black hairs'. Why, when **eyes** has -s? English sees the hair on your head as one whole thing, but you can count eyes: one eye, two **eyes**. (**a hair** is one single strand, *sehelai rambut*, for example in your food.)

id.text:
Bahasa Indonesia menaruh kata sifat **setelah** kata benda: *rambut panjang*. Bahasa Inggris menaruhnya **sebelum**: **She has long hair** (atau **Her hair is long**). Jangan 'She has hair long' atau 'She is long hair'.

Kalau ada dua kata sifat, urutannya tetap: **panjang-pendek dulu, warna terakhir**: **long black hair**, **short grey hair**. Kalau kamu menambah **straight** (*lurus*) atau **curly** (*keriting*), letaknya di tengah: **long straight black hair**.

**hair** (rambut di kepala) **tidak diberi -s**: *long black hair*, bukan 'long black hairs'. Kenapa **eyes** pakai -s? Bahasa Inggris melihat rambut di kepala sebagai satu kesatuan, tapi mata bisa dihitung: one eye, two **eyes**. (**a hair** artinya sehelai rambut, misalnya yang ada di makananmu.)

rows.en: My father has short grey hair.
Sari has curly hair and brown eyes.
rows.id: Rambut Sari keriting dan matanya cokelat.

id.note: juga benar: hair + is + kata sifat

blocks.text: Spelling: **grey** and **moustache** are British; American English writes **gray** and **mustache**. Both are correct and mean the same.

id.text: Ejaan: **grey** dan **moustache** adalah ejaan Inggris (British); bahasa Inggris Amerika menulis **gray** dan **mustache**. Keduanya benar dan artinya sama.

blocks.explain: The describing word goes **before** the noun: **long hair**. 'hair long' copies *rambut panjang*, and 'is long hair' uses be where English needs **has**.

id.explain: Kata sifat diletakkan **sebelum** kata benda: **long hair**. 'hair long' meniru *rambut panjang*, dan 'is long hair' memakai be padahal bahasa Inggris butuh **has**.

blocks.text: **Personality** (*sifat, kepribadian*) is what a person is like inside: how they act with other people. Here are eight useful words:

id.text: **Personality** (*sifat, kepribadian*) adalah seperti apa seseorang di dalam dirinya: bagaimana dia bersikap kepada orang lain. Ini delapan kata yang berguna:

blocks.text:
Use them in two ways:
- after **be**: *Bu Ani is **patient**.*
- before a noun (**person, man, woman, teacher**): then you need **a**: *She's **a** patient teacher.* With **very**: **a very friendly person**, never 'very friendly person'.

**a/an** looks at the **next word**: **an honest man** (*an*, because the h in *honest* is silent, so the word starts with an 'o' sound), but **a very honest man** (the next word is now *very*).

id.text:
Pakai dengan dua cara:
- setelah **be**: *Bu Ani is **patient**.*
- sebelum kata benda (**person, man, woman, teacher**): di sini kamu butuh **a**: *She's **a** patient teacher.* Dengan **very**: **a very friendly person**, jangan 'very friendly person'.

**a/an** melihat **kata berikutnya**: **an honest man** (*an*, karena h di *honest* tidak dibaca, jadi katanya diawali bunyi 'o'), tapi **a very honest man** (kata berikutnya sekarang *very*).

blocks.text:
Two Indonesian traps:
- *lucu* has two meanings. A person who makes you laugh is **funny**; a baby or a kitten is **cute**.
- *baik* for a person is **kind** or **nice**. 'She's good' usually means she's good at something (good at her job).
To be polite about bad points, make them softer: **a bit lazy**, **not very patient**.

id.text:
Dua jebakan dari bahasa Indonesia:
- *lucu* punya dua arti. Orang yang bikin kamu tertawa itu **funny**; bayi atau anak kucing yang menggemaskan itu **cute**.
- *baik* untuk orang adalah **kind** atau **nice**. 'She's good' biasanya berarti dia pandai dalam sesuatu (good at her job).
Supaya sopan saat membicarakan sifat buruk, buat lebih halus: **a bit lazy** (*agak malas*), **not very patient** (*kurang sabar*).

blocks.explain: With a noun (person) you need **a**, and a/an goes before **very**: **a very patient person**. Without the noun, there's no a: *Pak Hasan is very patient.*

id.explain: Dengan kata benda (person) kamu butuh **a**, dan a/an diletakkan sebelum **very**: **a very patient person**. Tanpa kata benda, tidak ada a: *Pak Hasan is very patient.*

material.title: What does she look like? or What is she like?

blocks.text:
These two questions look almost the same, but they ask different things:
- **What does she look like?** asks about **appearance** (*penampilannya seperti apa?*). Answer: *She's tall and she has curly hair.*
- **What is she like?** (short: **What's she like?**) asks about **personality**: what kind of person she is (*orangnya seperti apa?*). Answer: *She's friendly and very funny.*

In both questions **like** doesn't mean *suka*: it means *seperti*. Don't mix them up with **What does she like?** = *Dia suka apa?* Answer: *She likes music.*

id.text:
Dua pertanyaan ini kelihatan hampir sama, tapi menanyakan hal yang berbeda:
- **What does she look like?** menanyakan **penampilan** (*penampilannya seperti apa?*). Jawaban: *She's tall and she has curly hair.*
- **What is she like?** (pendeknya: **What's she like?**) menanyakan **sifat**: orang seperti apa dia (*orangnya seperti apa?*). Jawaban: *She's friendly and very funny.*

Di kedua pertanyaan ini **like** tidak berarti *suka*, tapi *seperti*. Jangan tertukar dengan **What does she like?** = *Dia suka apa?* Jawaban: *She likes music.*

rows.en: What does your new colleague look like? — He's short and he wears glasses.
rows.id: Rekan kerja barumu penampilannya seperti apa? — Dia pendek dan pakai kacamata.

rows.en: What's your teacher like? — She's kind and very patient.

rows.en: What does Budi like? — He likes badminton.

rows.note: look like + a person = look similar

blocks.text: Answer **What does she look like?** with **is** and **has**, not with *look like* again: *She's tall*, not 'She looks like tall'. Use **looks like + a person** only for *mirip*: *Rina looks like her mother.*

id.text: Jawab **What does she look like?** dengan **is** dan **has**, bukan dengan *look like* lagi: *She's tall*, bukan 'She looks like tall'. Pakai **looks like + orang** hanya untuk *mirip*: *Rina looks like her mother.*

options: She's short and she has curly hair.
blocks.explain: **look like** asks about appearance, so the answer describes her body and hair. 'She's very kind' answers *What is she like?*, and 'She likes K-pop' answers *What does she like?*

id.prompt: Pilih jawaban yang tepat: 'What does your sister look like?' — '___'
id.explain: **look like** menanyakan penampilan, jadi jawabannya menggambarkan badan dan rambutnya. 'She's very kind' menjawab *What is she like?*, dan 'She likes K-pop' menjawab *What does she like?*

id.title: What does she look like? atau What is she like?

blocks.text:
Use the rules from the comparatives lesson:
- short words: **-er + than**: tall → **taller than**, young → **younger than**, kind → **kinder than**. long → **longer**: *Sari has **longer** hair than her sister* (it still goes before *hair*).
- 2 beats ending in -y: y → **-ier**: funny → **funnier**.
- longer words: **more**: **more patient**, **more honest**.
- the same: **as … as** (*se-*): *Dimas is **as tall as** his father.* Less: **not as … as**.
- *paling*: **the tallest** in my family, **the funniest** person in the office.

After **than** we usually say **me, him, her**: *My brother is taller than **me**.* (*than I am* is also correct.)

id.text:
Pakai aturan dari pelajaran perbandingan:
- kata pendek: **-er + than**: tall → **taller than**, young → **younger than**, kind → **kinder than**. long → **longer**: *Sari has **longer** hair than her sister* (tetap diletakkan sebelum *hair*).
- 2 ketukan berakhiran -y: y → **-ier**: funny → **funnier**.
- kata yang lebih panjang: **more**: **more patient**, **more honest**.
- sama: **as … as** (*se-*): *Dimas is **as tall as** his father.* Kurang: **not as … as**.
- *paling*: **the tallest** in my family, **the funniest** person in the office.

Setelah **than** biasanya kita pakai **me, him, her**: *My brother is taller than **me**.* (*than I am* juga benar.)

rows.en: My brother is two years older than me.
rows.id: Kakakku dua tahun lebih tua daripada aku.

rows.en: Sari is kinder than her cousin.
rows.id: Sari lebih baik hati daripada sepupunya.

rows.en: My mother is more patient than my father.
I'm not as tall as my sister.
Dimas is the funniest person in our office.
rows.id: Dimas orang paling lucu di kantor kami.

blocks.text: *kakak* and *adik* don't say if the person is a man or a woman, but English does, and it uses the comparative for the age: **older sister** = *kakak perempuan*, **younger brother** = *adik laki-laki*.

id.text: *kakak* dan *adik* tidak menunjukkan laki-laki atau perempuan, tapi bahasa Inggris menunjukkannya, dan memakai bentuk perbandingan untuk umurnya: **older sister** = *kakak perempuan*, **younger brother** = *adik laki-laki*.

blocks.text: A few personality words have two possible forms (friendly → friendlier or more friendly). Both are fine. In this lesson, compare with the clear ones: taller, younger, kinder, funnier, more patient.

id.text: Beberapa kata sifat punya dua bentuk (friendly → friendlier atau more friendly). Keduanya benar. Di pelajaran ini, bandingkan dengan kata yang jelas aturannya: taller, younger, kinder, funnier, more patient.

blocks.prompt: My father is ___ than my mother.
blocks.explain: **old** is short (1 beat), so it takes **-er**: **older than**. 'more old' uses the long-word rule, and 'oldest' is for *paling* (with the).

id.prompt: Lengkapi: My father is ___ than my mother.
id.explain: **old** kata pendek (1 ketukan), jadi pakai **-er**: **older than**. 'more old' memakai aturan kata panjang, dan 'oldest' untuk *paling* (dengan the).
